Goal: In MVFA's few-shot inference, the released code min-max normalises the zero-shot (text) branch and the few-shot (memory-bank) branch with the minimum and maximum over the entire test set and adds them with a fixed weight of 0.5, so the score of one image depends on the rest of the test set and a single incoming image cannot be scored. Can this transductive normalisation be replaced by an inductive one computed only from the K normal support images, at a small cost in AUROC? The inductive normaliser maps each branch's patch scores through the 1st and 99th percentiles of the leave-one-out patch scores of the supports (every patch of support i scored against the memory bank of the other K-1 supports and against the text anchors), which gives thousands of reference values even at K = 2; the fusion weight and the max pooling of the image score are kept fixed. Primary outcome: image-level and pixel-level AUROC of inductive versus transductive normalisation on each held-out BMAD dataset for K in {2, 4, 8, 16}. Motivating measurement: the spread of the original method's AUROC across random half-size test subsets and at shifted prevalence (10% and 50% abnormal). Secondary outcome: sensitivity at 95% specificity with a threshold fixed from the support scores alone.

Code-verified facts about the public code of the source paper (github.com/MediaBrain-SJTU/MVFA-AD):
- CLIP/adapter.py: CLIP_Inplanted wraps a frozen CLIP ViT-L/14-336 (input 240x240); ClipAdapter bottleneck adapters are inserted after layers [6, 12, 18, 24]; there are two adapter sets, seg_adapters (segmentation branch) and det_adapters (detection branch), mixed residually with ratio 0.1.

Hypothesis to revise: TITLE: Conformal thresholds on residual-CDF scores
SUMMARY: Normalise each branch with the residual empirical CDF and set the operating threshold as a split-conformal quantile of the supports' leave-one-out image scores, giving an anatomy-aware inductive score and a distribution-free false-positive bound.
HYPOTHESIS: On held-out BMAD datasets with K >= 8, residual-CDF scoring with a conformal threshold at alpha = 0.1 keeps realised false-positive rate at or below alpha + 1/(K+1) and achieves at least 3 points higher sensitivity than the same conformal threshold on globally normalised scores.
RATIONALE: The conformal parent guarantees a false-positive bound for any per-image score, but the power of the resulting test (its sensitivity) depends on how well the score separates abnormal from normal images. The residual-CDF parent produces a more separating score on aligned modalities by removing anatomy offsets. Combining them keeps the guarantee and raises the sensitivity at the guaranteed false-positive rate.
METHOD: 1) Residual CDF per branch and level as in the parent (exact leave-one-out construction). 2) Fused map with 0.5 weights; image score = max. 3) LOO image scores of the K supports; tau = sorted(s)[ceil((K+1)(1 - alpha)) - 1]. 4) Report realised FPR and sensitivity at alpha in {0.1, 0.2}. No training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baseline: conformal threshold on global-CDF scores. Metrics: realised FPR vs. bound, sensitivity, AUROC. Falsified if sensitivity is not higher than with global-CDF scores at equal guaranteed FPR.
